verses.text: But now men younger than me laugh at me, men whose fathers I wouldn’t even have put with my sheepdogs.
What good was their strength to me? Their vigor had already worn away.
Starving and gaunt, they gnaw at the dry ground in the gloom of a desolate wasteland.
They pick salty plants by the bushes and eat the roots of broom trees.
People drive them out and shout after them as if they were thieves.
They live in frightening ravines, in holes in the ground and in the rocks.
They bray among the bushes and huddle beneath the nettles.
They are children of fools and of the wicked, whipped out of the land.
Now they make songs about me. My name has become a joke to them.
They can’t stand me. They keep their distance and think nothing of spitting in my face.
God loosened his cord and brought me low, and now they hold nothing back around me.
A mob rises up at my right. They knock my feet out from under me and pile up ramps to attack me.
They tear up my path and push me toward ruin without anyone’s help.
They surge in as if through a wide gap in a wall, rolling in through the wreckage.
Terrors close in on me. They sweep my honor away like the wind, and my well-being vanishes like a cloud.
Now my life is draining away. Days of suffering have taken hold of me.
At night my bones feel pierced, and the pain that gnaws at me never lets up.
A great force twists my clothes and grips me like the collar of my tunic.
God has thrown me into the mud. I’ve become like dust and ashes.
I cry out to you, but you don’t answer. I stand up, and you just look at me.
You’ve turned cruel toward me. With all your strength you come after me.
You lift me into the wind and drive me along with it. You toss me until I fall apart in the storm.
I know you’ll bring me to death, the home set aside for everyone who lives.
Doesn’t a person reach out a hand when they fall? Don’t they cry for help when disaster strikes?
Didn’t I cry for people in trouble? Didn’t my heart ache for those in need?
I looked for good, but trouble came. I waited for light, but darkness came.
My heart churns and can’t settle down. Days of suffering have come for me.
I walk around in mourning, with no sunlight. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
I’ve become a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.
My skin darkens and peels, and my bones burn with heat.
My harp now plays songs of mourning, and my flute sounds like people weeping.
